title: No Gaining Idea
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett takes up Suzuki Roshi's passage on practice without gaining ideas from Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind, read alongside the Heart Sutra's line that form is form and emptiness is emptiness. Nomon sets the book against the earlier Zen of D.T. Suzuki and Philip Kapleau's Three Pillars of Zen, with its dramatic awakenings, and adds the Three Doors of Liberation, especially wishlessness. The story of Baoshou fanning himself from Genjokoan asks why practice continues when the wind already reaches everywhere. Nomon ends with a flash of jealousy on Facebook over a friend's retreat at Hollyhock, which tightens, then releases into freedom again.
